main_body: Sci-fi control tower: antenna on a sloped upper roof, a window band, a narrow grey shaft with two screens, a wide sloped lower skirt roof, and a base with a door and yellow hazard stripes
top_band: Upper roof slope at x=24: blue-grey rows 8-14 (L118-148), lightest edge rows 15-16 (L178), about 9 rows. The lower skirt roof at rows 52-62 has the same structure.
evidence: Both roofs read as sloped trapezoids with a lighter top band and a lightest front-edge row (rows 15-16, L178). A step then leads into dark rows 18-21 (L34), which act as an eave shadow over the window band, whose front face runs rows 18-29. The windows and screens have dark inset frames. The lower skirt roof (rows 52-62) sits above the base wall (rows 63+) in the same way. Both major parts follow the 3/4 contract, and no receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The outline is near-black, with 84% of dark edge pixels neutral (the references are 7-9%). This is the sticker-like outline the Beodeul standard avoids. Flat-fill coverage is 21% against 0% for both references, and the shaft, the dark base and the window band are large areas of one flat colour. The piece has only 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The median of 10 colours per tile is comparable to the stone reference, and the roofs have some panel lines, so the shading is acceptable. The black outline and the flat fills still make it look thinner and flatter than the references.
